method: Each issue contains only material that had been published by the last day of its month. Sources carry their own availability dates: news by publication, city records by the date the city posted them, HCD annual report rows by the release of that reporting year, Zillow by the month it published, ACS by its December release, RHNA progress by its August 2026 vintage.

lede: 171 items entered the public record across the nine Bay Area counties in September 2026: 125 housing, 14 development, 4 transportation, 28 civic.
Of the 101 jurisdictions this dashboard tracks, 100 had a published Zillow index; their median typical home stood at $1.24M in the 2026 index, the most recent available when this issue went out.

sections.title: Across the nine counties
paragraphs: San Mateo County accounted for the most of it, with 37 items; every county produced something.

sections.title: The twelve months behind this issue
paragraphs: In the twelve months to September 30, 2026, 466 published reports about these nine counties reached this dashboard - 246 on housing, 81 on development, 32 on transportation, 107 on civic, alongside 1,192 dated city and state records.

Most of that coverage came from San Mateo (133), Santa Clara (105), Contra Costa (63), Alameda (55). Coverage is not the same as activity: a county with fewer reports may simply have fewer newsrooms filing to the sources this dashboard reads.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,792 developments carrying 76,796 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into.

sections.title: The twelve months behind this issue
paragraphs: In the twelve months to July 31, 2026, 237 published reports about these nine counties reached this dashboard - 104 on housing, 49 on development, 19 on transportation, 65 on civic, alongside 1,558 dated city and state records.

Most of that coverage came from San Mateo (66), Santa Clara (65), Contra Costa (28), Alameda (27). Coverage is not the same as activity: a county with fewer reports may simply have fewer newsrooms filing to the sources this dashboard reads.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,791 developments carrying 76,795 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into.
